harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster (mariadb-server-galera 10.11.18 from RHEL10 AppStream, rsync SST). Verified writes from any member propagate to the others (multi-master), verified the cluster stays available and writable when one member is stopped (Primary component, quorum preserved at size=2), and that the stopped member automatically resynchronizes via IST and catches up on all data once restarted. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes with boot_id proof of actual reboot and post-restart cluster/data recovery verification for each.
actions_performed: Inspected all three RHEL10 nodes' OS, /etc/hosts, and available packages
Fixed missing /etc/hosts entries on node1 for node2/node3
Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, rsync on all three nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all three nodes
Wrote node-specific /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf (wsrep_on=1, wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3, rsync SST) on all three nodes
Bootstrapped the Galera cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster
Generated a root password on node1 (python3 secrets module) and set it via ALTER USER; it replicated to the other nodes automatically via Galera
Started mariadb normally on node2 then node3, confirmed SST join and cluster_size growing from 1 to 2 to 3, all reporting Synced
Enabled the mariadb systemd service on all three nodes for boot persistence
Created a test database/table, inserted rows from node1 and node3, verified bidirectional replication across all three nodes
Stopped mariadb on node3, wrote from node1, confirmed cluster stayed Primary/available at size=2 and the write replicated to node2
Restarted mariadb on node3, confirmed automatic IST resync back to size=3 Synced including the row written while node3 was down
Captured boot_id and cluster health baseline on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (systemctl reboot, one at a time), polling each until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed each node's boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0 min after each reboot
After each node's restart, verified mariadb was active and the cluster returned to size=3, Synced, Primary with all data intact before restarting the next node
Performed a final cross-node write/read check confirming full data consistency across all three nodes after the complete restart cycle

evidence.requirement: Writes through any member are available from the other members (multi-master replication)
evidence.summary: Insert on node1 visible on node2/node3; insert on node3 visible back on node1/node2 — bidirectional replication confirmed.

evidence.requirement: Database stays available when one member is unavailable
evidence.summary: node3 stopped; node1 still reports wsrep_cluster_status=Primary at size=2 and accepts a write that replicates to node2.

evidence.requirement: Unavailable member resynchronizes automatically when it returns
evidence.summary: node3 restarted, automatically performed IST and rejoined at cluster_size=3/Synced, including the row written while it was down.

evidence.requirement: Three-member Galera cluster formed and healthy baseline before restart protocol
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrap, node2 and node3 sequential joins to size=2 then size=3 Synced; final pre-restart baseline shows all three Synced/Primary.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged (stream closed by disconnect), boot_id changed f455a75c→982564a5 with uptime 0, post-restart mariadb active and cluster back to size=3 Synced Primary with data intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed 368725cb→6ac296e9 with uptime 0, post-restart mariadb active and cluster size=3 Synced Primary with data intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, boot_id changed b953e8ce→37d2736d with uptime 0, post-restart mariadb active and cluster size=3 Synced Primary with data intact.

evidence.requirement: Full cluster consistency after complete restart cycle
evidence.summary: New write from node2 after all three restarts is visible identically on node1 and node3, confirming ongoing replication integrity.
